_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@1f7949c87ff7: Treaty conformity — OK conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OK income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OK return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Oklahoma's resident return (Form 511) starts at line 1 from "Federal adjusted gross income (from Federal 1040 or 1040-SR)" and then applies Schedule 511-A (Oklahoma subtractions) and Schedule 511-B (Oklahoma additions) to arrive at Oklahoma AGI. The complete Schedule 511-B additions list for 2023 is closed and enumerated: (1) state and municipal bond interest, (2) out-of-state losses, (3) lump-sum distributions not in federal AGI, (4) federal net operating loss, (5) recapture of depletion / excess federal depletion, (6) recapture of 529 contributions, (7) Oklahoma loss distributed by an electing PTE, (8) miscellaneous other additions. There is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income anywhere in the resident or nonresident packets (a full-text search of both 2023 packets for "treaty"/"treaties" returns zero hits). Because OK begins from federal AGI and does not add treaty income back (unlike CA Schedule CA), federally treaty-exempt income already excluded from federal AGI flows through and is NOT re-taxed by Oklahoma. The 511-NR likewise begins from the federal amounts: "The Federal Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) will be adjusted using the Oklahoma additions and subtractions." Therefore conforms = true.
_strings.@@3485434fac88: Oklahoma Earned Income Credit (EIC) — Resident and part-year resident filers who qualify for the federal Earned Income Credit. Nonresidents do not qualify. The federal EIC is recalculated using the federal EITC eligibility/computation rules in effect for the 2020 tax year. A copy of the federal return and OTC Form 511-EIC must be provided.
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@4e50d2001477: Sales Tax Relief Credit (Sales Tax Refund) — Must be an Oklahoma resident for the entire year. General income limit is $20,000 of total gross household income, raised to $50,000 if any one of the following applies: you can claim an exemption for a dependent; you and/or your spouse are 65 or older by 12/31/2023; or you have a physical disability constituting a substantial handicap to employment (proof required). Excluded: anyone who received TANF in any month of 2023; felons who were DOC inmates for any part of the year; and individuals living in Oklahoma under a visa. Claimed on Form 538-S.

_strings.@@a374892a89c9: Credit for Property Tax Relief (Low Income Property Tax Credit) — Any person 65 years of age or older, or any totally disabled person, who is head of a household and was a resident of and domiciled in Oklahoma during the entire preceding calendar year, and whose gross household income for that year does not exceed $12,000. The claim is for property taxes paid on the household occupied during the preceding calendar year. Claim must be made on Form 538-H.

Must provide a copy of the federal return and, if applicable, the federal child care credit schedule.

Tax line: Form 511, line 14(a): 'Oklahoma Income Tax from Tax Table (see pages 27-38 of instructions)', computed on line 13 'Oklahoma Taxable Income (line 9 minus line 12)', where line 12 = 'Total deductions and exemptions (add lines 10 and 11 or amount from Sch. 511-E, line 5)'. Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,000 — 'Special' additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer/spouse who is 65 or older at the close of the tax year, allowed ONLY if Form 511 line 1 Federal AGI does not exceed: $15,000 single / $25,000 joint / $12,500 married filing separate / $19,000 head of household (Roth-conversion income is excluded when testing these limits). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — if eligible, claim it in the exemption boxes at the top of Form 511 and it flows into line 11.); blind ($1,000 — Additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer/spouse who is legally blind; part of the top-of-form exemption count flowing into Form 511 line 11. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — claim it on the form.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Form 511, line 9 'Oklahoma income after adjustments (line 7 minus line 8)'. Line 1 starts from federal AGI; lines 2-8 apply Oklahoma subtractions (Schedule 511-A), out-of-state income (line 4), Oklahoma additions (Schedule 511-B) and Oklahoma adjustments (Schedule 511-C) to reach line 9. The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Form 511 line 10) and $1,000 per exemption/dependent (Form 511 line 11) to reproduce line 13 'Oklahoma Taxable Income', and applies the brackets to reproduce line 14a. Do NOT pre-subtract deductions or exemptions from the figure you supply. If Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income) is more than zero, or you itemize, the shipped fixed deduction/exemption amounts do not apply — see notes. Tax Table mandate below $100,000: Form 511 line 14a instructs 'Using Form 511, line 13, find your tax in the Tax Table (pages 27-38)'. The table's $50-wide bands compute tax at the band midpoint, so plain bracket math may differ from the table by a few dollars within a band (e.g., the packet's example: MFJ taxable income $14,793 -> table tax $347; exact bracket math gives $348). The filed form must use the table below $100,000. Taxable income of $100,000 or more uses the packet's page 38 worksheets: Single/MFS tax = $4,562 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000; MFJ/HOH/Qualified Widow(er) tax = $4,395 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000. Printed worksheet constants vs exact bracket sums: the MFJ/HOH/QW constant $4,395 exactly equals the cumulative bracket sum at $100,000; the Single/MFS constant $4,562 is the exact cumulative sum $4,561.50 rounded up $0.50, so above $100,000 the form worksheet can come out $1 higher than exact marginal bracket math after whole-dollar rounding. Bracket schedule source: the 2023 Form 511 packet prints only the Tax Table and the $100,000+ worksheets, not a marginal rate schedule. The brackets shipped here are copied verbatim from 68 O.S. § 2355(C) as in force for tax year 2023 ('For all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2022'; version whose amendment history ends with Laws 2022, SB 1802, superseded effective January 1, 2024 by Laws 2023, 1st Extr. Sess., HB 1040X), archived on the official Oklahoma State Courts Network: https://www.oscn.net/applications/oscn/DeliverDocument.asp?CiteID=494781 . Every bracket boundary was cross-checked against the packet's printed table rows and worksheet constants. WARNING for future maintainers: the CURRENT OSCN text of 68 O.S. § 2355 (as rewritten in 2025) restates subsection C as 'For tax years 2024 and 2025' and widens the MFJ/HOH 3.75% band to 'next $4,600.00' — that text does NOT reproduce the 2023 (or the OTC-printed) table and must not be used for tax year 2023; use the archived version cited above. One schedule covers Single and Married Filing Separately (identical thresholds — 68 O.S. § 2355(C)(1)); a second schedule covers Married Filing Jointly, surviving spouse, AND Head of Household (68 O.S. § 2355(C)(2)) — HOH is NOT a separate schedule; it is duplicated from MFJ here. The tax table likewise has only two columns: 'Single or married filing separate' and 'Married filing joint or head of household'. Qualifying widow(er)/surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column and schedule (tax table footnote: 'This column must also be used by a Qualified Widow(er)'; the statute includes surviving spouses in the MFJ paragraph) — the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is correct for Oklahoma. Out-of-state income gate: if Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income, except wages) is more than zero, do NOT complete lines 10-11 — Schedule 511-E prorates deductions and exemptions instead, so the fixed standard deduction and $1,000 exemptions shipped here do not apply; compute on the form. Itemizers: if you claimed itemized deductions on your federal return you MUST claim Oklahoma itemized deductions (Schedule 511-D) instead of the standard deduction; Oklahoma itemized deductions are capped at $17,000 (charitable contributions and medical expenses are not subject to the cap). The shipped standard deduction applies only to federal standard-deduction claimants. You qualify for the Oklahoma standard deduction even when claimed as a dependent on another return. Form 511 line 14b add-ons are NOT modeled: the additional 10% tax on nonqualified Health Savings Account withdrawals, recapture of the Oklahoma Affordable Housing Tax Credit, and IRC Section 965(h) installment payments. Farm Income Averaging (Form 573, entered on line 14a with a '1' in the box) is also not modeled. Oklahoma's personal/dependent allowances are true income-base exemptions (Form 511 line 11 is subtracted from income before the rate applies via lines 12-13), not tax credits. Separately, Oklahoma's Child Care/Child Tax Credit (line 15, Schedule 511-F), Oklahoma EIC (line 28, Schedule 511-G), Sales Tax Relief Credit (line 25, Form 538-S) and Property Tax Relief credit (line 24, Form 538-H) are CREDITS against tax and are not part of this computation. All Form 511 money entries are whole dollars ('00' boxes); the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches the form's presentation.
